Hi Tom / Claire,

Great to meet earlier - thanks for walking through your end-to-end flow. Per our call, I wanted to capture the proposed POC plan and the capacity asks so we can align on success criteria and next steps. Please review and flag anything I missed.

Summary / success criteria (what Acme AI needs to validate):
- Functional: generated responses meet target latency (p50 < 250ms) and quality on the 50-item test prompts you shared.
- Performance: sustain 20 concurrent LLM requests at median seq len 512 without degradation; handle bursts up to 60 concurrent (short spikes).
- Cost/ops: confirm inference cost per 1k tokens and autoscaling behaves within agreed budget window.

POC capacity proposal (suggested):
- Reserved baseline: 3 x A100 GPUs (reserved pool) for steady-state throughput.
- Autoscaling: allow burst-to 6 GPUs for short spikes (10-15 minute windows); target scale-up within 60s.
- Networking/region: run in us-west-2 for lowest latency to your services.

Evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0: contract + SOW + kickoff (sign by Fri 3/26)
- Week 1: infra provisioning, model pinning, integration support (SE onboarding)
- Weeks 2-4: run test harness, live traffic ramp, measure SLOs and cost metrics
- End of Week 4: joint review vs success criteria and decision to convert to Dedicated or iterate.

Ownership / contacts:
- Redwood AE: me (Marissa) - commercial and scheduling
- Redwood SE: Dev Patel - infra config, autoscaling rules, monitoring
- Acme AI: Tom Benson - product owner; Claire Li - infra lead

Attachments: redwood-poc-capacity-proposal.pdf (details + cost estimate), redwood-poc-tpl.xlsx (test harness / metrics dashboard template).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the success criteria above and the proposed baseline/burst capacity.
2) If confirmed, we’ll send an SOW/DocuSign for the 4-week POC and get SE hours on the calendar.

Thanks - happy to jump on another 30-min sync if helpful.

Hi Tom / Claire - thanks for the quick reply and the traffic numbers. Technical notes and recommendation below.

Short answers:
- Reserved baseline: 3 x A100 will likely meet sustained throughput for 15-20 concurrent at seq len ~480 with efficient batching.
- If you want headroom and easier ramp we can do 4 x A100 reserved as you requested; autoscale policy can add up to +4 GPUs (so 8 total) for burst windows.
- Scale-up latency: typical cold-scale to add a GPU is ~45-90s depending on region and VM warm pools; we recommend pre-warming if you expect predictable scheduled spikes.

Monitoring & evaluation metrics (what we’ll instrument for the POC):
- p50/p95 generation latency, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, queue length, cache hit rate (prefix KV), batching stats, and cost per 1k tokens.
- Alerts we recommend: sustained GPU util >85% for >5m, queue length >X, and scale failures.

Autoscaling policy suggestion:
- Target: maintain p95 < 500ms.
- Min: reserved pool (3 or 4 GPUs)
- Scale-up: add GPUs if queue length > 50 or p95 > 500ms for 60s; step by 1-2 GPUs with cooldown 90s.
- Scale-down: reduce when GPU util < 30% for 5m, cooldown 5m.

Test harness: we’ll run your 50-item prompt set plus a 24-hour simulated traffic run at peak QPS to validate cost. I attached the capacity proposal PDF with estimates - see redwood-poc-capacity-proposal.pdf.

Happy to jump on the kickoff tech call; available Thu/Fri afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
